item.title: OpenAI CEO says world 'should accept some bad things happening' for AI benefits
item.description:
## Former Anthropic researcher reveals ‘two things I saw that made me scared’ about AI Former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher [Jacob Coxon](https://www.foxnews.com/tech/ai-newsletter-researcher-delivers-extinction-warning) told New York City lawmakers Monday that there were “two things I saw that made me scared” about the development of artificial intelligence.
## Threat report uncovers attempts to use AI for ‘biologically risky’ activities: Anthropic A recent threat intelligence report found that individuals have attempted to use artificial intelligence for potentially dangerous biological activities, an Anthropic leader said Monday.
## Google says 'if it's illegal without AI, it's still illegal with AI' Google told New York City lawmakers that existing laws should apply to [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence), declaring that “if it’s illegal without AI, it’s still illegal with AI.”
## Ex-Google DeepMind researcher warns AI could become ‘everyone’s adversary’ A former [Google DeepMind](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/companies/google) safety researcher warned New York City lawmakers that the race to develop increasingly powerful artificial intelligence could create an adversary of its own.
## OpenAI CEO says 'world should accept some bad things' for AI benefits OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said [artificial intelligence](https://www.foxnews.com/category/tech/artificial-intelligence) should remain widely available, arguing the technology's benefits are worth accepting some risks.

item.title: ‘That is recklessness’: Florida's staunch GOP AI opponents slam Altman's ‘bad things’ comments
item.description:
# ‘That is recklessness’: Florida's staunch GOP AI opponents slam Altman's ‘bad things’ comments ## Share TALLAHASSEE, Florida — Florida Republican leaders are panning OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s comments that “the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits” of artificial intelligence development at large, continuing their hardline stances against the industry at large.
Florida, through proposed legislation and legal actions by Uthmeier, is fighting to install new guardrails around artificial intelligence and is even attempting to stop OpenAI from further developing its technology while a court battle between the tech giant and Sunshine State plays out.

item.title: AI apocalypse? Most Louisiana candidates for Congress stay vague on regulation
item.description:
Most candidates running for Congress in Louisiana agree there should be some federal regulations placed on artificial intelligence.
Lead tech executives, [including Microsoft founder Bill Gates](https://www.gatesnotes.com/a-turbulent-ai-era-and-critical-choices-to-make), have warned that artificial intelligence could upend the job market and pose significant threats to public safety and infrastructure unless it is safely contained.
Democrats expressed more concern about the impact of artificial intelligence, particularly on the job market and the economy.
Senate, said companies that use artificial intelligence to cut jobs should not receive a tax break for doing so.
In addition to Gates saying that artificial intelligence could cause “a billion” deaths, a former researcher for two of the most high-profile AI companies issued a similar warning.
Echols said Congress should proceed with caution when it comes to artificial intelligence, but he added that he didn’t put much stock in warnings from Gates, whose reputation he considers tarnished since his relationship with deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein has come to light.
Garcia and Pat Forbes, a Democrat running in the 6th District, said they don’t have the expertise to determine whether artificial intelligence could threaten humanity.
